headline_marked: Country music legend [[Dolly Parton dies at 80]]
headline: Country music legend Dolly Parton dies at 80
summary: The iconic singer, songwriter, and actress sold over 100 million records and won 11 Grammy awards throughout her six-decade career.
details: Dolly Parton, the irrepressible queen of country music, has died at the age of 80. Her family confirmed the news in a statement on Tuesday.
Born into a 'dirt-poor' family in Tennessee as one of 12 children, Parton rose from humble beginnings to become one of the best-selling female artists of all time.
She is remembered for timeless hits like 'Jolene,' 'I Will Always Love You,' and 'Coat of Many Colors,' selling over 100 million records and winning 11 Grammy awards.
Beyond music, Parton was a versatile entertainer who starred in movies, hosted a TV variety show, and founded the popular Dollywood theme park in Tennessee.
She was widely admired for her philanthropy, donating $1 million to Vanderbilt University for Covid-19 vaccine research and establishing literacy programs for preschool children.
Parton's ability to connect with people across political divides in a polarized America was fueled by her nonpartisanship and commitment to her working-class roots.
Her legacy includes a life-size statue in her home county of Tennessee, though she famously declined a statue in Nashville in 2021 to avoid being put on a 'pedestal'.
caption:
From a one-room cabin to global superstardom, the queen of country music has left us.

Dolly Parton, the irrepressible queen of country music, has died at the age of 80. Her family confirmed the news in a statement on Tuesday.

Born into a 'dirt-poor' family in Tennessee as one of 12 children, Parton rose from humble beginnings to become one of the best-selling female artists of all time.

She is remembered for timeless hits like 'Jolene,' 'I Will Always Love You,' and 'Coat of Many Colors,' selling over 100 million records and winning 11 Grammy awards.

Beyond music, Parton was a versatile entertainer who starred in movies, hosted a TV variety show, and founded the popular Dollywood theme park in Tennessee.

She was widely admired for her philanthropy, donating $1 million to Vanderbilt University for Covid-19 vaccine research and establishing literacy programs for preschool children.

Parton's ability to connect with people across political divides in a polarized America was fueled by her nonpartisanship and commitment to her working-class roots.

Her legacy includes a life-size statue in her home county of Tennessee, though she famously declined a statue in Nashville in 2021 to avoid being put on a 'pedestal'.

headline_marked: Canada [[unveils 15-50% counter-tariffs]] on US goods in trade war
headline: Canada unveils 15-50% counter-tariffs on US goods in trade war
summary: Ottawa responds to Donald Trump's duties with retaliatory taxes on steel, dairy, and electronics, while providing a $5.4 billion aid package for local firms.
details: Canada has announced counter-tariffs on US goods ranging from 15 to 50 percent, intensifying a trade war between the two close allies. The measures will take effect on September 8, following US President Donald Trump's 50-percent duties.

Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne stated that the retaliatory tariffs match US levels and will impact industries including steel, dairy, and electronics. Affected goods include frozen and fresh fish, dishwashers, washing machines, and railway construction materials.

To support affected businesses, the Canadian government has announced a $5.4 billion (CA$7.5 billion) aid package for firms and workers. Industry Minister Melanie Joly vowed to work with new trading partners and promised further action if US tariffs on Canadian autos rise to 50 percent.
The conflict stems from the collapse of trade negotiations. Trump's latest tariffs hit approximately $20 billion in Canadian goods, representing 5.5 percent of Canada's exports to the United States.

Under the planned response, US steel and aluminum products previously taxed at 25 percent will now face 50 percent tariffs. Other goods like cheese and certain appliances will face 25 percent duties, while electric equipment and tools will see a 15 percent duty.

Tensions have escalated beyond trade, with Donald Trump suggesting Canada could become the 51st US state and considering renaming Lake Ontario as 'Lake America.' Ontario Premier Doug Ford has sharply criticized these threats.

The United States remains Canada's largest trading partner, with Canadian exports to the US accounting for 70 percent of its overall total. Polling shows Canadians broadly support the government's decision to walk away from talks.
